name: Chelsea Bun
desc: A sticky spiral of currants and spice, glazed in syrup. Cambridge has queued for them on Trumpington Street since 1920. Restores 160 HP.

name: Smoked Fen Eel
desc: Ely means eel island, and the monks once took their rent in eels. Rich, smoky and oily. Restores 200 HP.

name: Norfolk Dumpling
desc: No suet, just flour, water and a little yeast. Norfolk folk call them swimmers, because they float. Restores 150 HP.

name: Norwich Mustard
desc: Bright yellow, milled in Norwich since 1814. One dab up the nose and nobody stays asleep, cold or confused for long.

name: Fen Runners
desc: Long, flat-bladed skates strapped to your boots, as raced on the frozen Fens for prizes of a leg of mutton.
msg: {name} came skating in on its Fen Runners!

name: Punt Pole Tip
desc: The lucky ash tip off a Cambridge punt pole, given by the Punt Captain. Stand on the till end, like a civilised person.
msg: {name}'s Punt Pole Tip pushed it along!

name: Trinity Pippin
desc: A small, hard apple from the orchard at Trinity. Not Newton's, but it has clearly been thinking about gravity.
effect_text: Lore up when it first comes out.
msg: {name}'s Trinity Pippin gave it a bright idea!

name: Double Helix Pin
desc: A little gold twisted ladder from behind the bar at the Eagle. Each strand can rebuild the other: that's how life mends itself.
msg: {name}'s Double Helix Pin knitted it back together a bit.

name: Canary Scarf
desc: Yellow and green, for Norwich City and the canaries the Strangers brought in 1565. On the ball, City.
effect_text: Speed up when it first comes out.
msg: {name}'s Canary Scarf had it off like a shot!

name: Norfolk Reed
desc: Cut from the Broads and the Fens in winter. The finest thatching reed in Britain: a good roof lasts fifty years or more.

name: Newton's Apple
desc: Fallen from the tree outside Trinity, grown from Newton's own tree at Woolsthorpe. It did not hit anybody on the head.
